raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Moves ROCm FP8 ViT attention onto AITER's assembly FP8 kernel for vision towers with head_dim 80 (e.g. MiniMax-M3), and makes static FP8 scale calibration reliable with a data-parallel encoder. Three small code commits (the padding is opt-in) and two test commits.

| # | Commit | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Pad FP8 ViT attention head_dim to 128 (`VLLM_ROCM_VIT_FP8_PAD_HEAD_DIM=128`; default 16, unchanged) | Padding head_dim 80 only to a multiple of 16 keeps the encoder off AITER's hd128 FP8 kernel |
| 2 | Write the FP8 ViT scale file atomically; optional rewrite at every amax wrap (`VLLM_MM_ENCODER_FP8_SCALE_SAVE_EVERY_WRAP`, default off) | With `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data`, every rank writes `mm_encoder_fp8_scale_save_path` at the same time, so a reader can see a torn file. The rewrite option lets a calibration run end with the scales of its last window. |
| 3 | Pass 1-element FP8 descales to AITER as shape `(1,)` | Shape `(1,1,1,1)` makes AITER pick its CK-tile kernel instead of the asm FP8 kernel (same math) |
| 4 | Run the FP8 ViT scale tests on ROCm; test the atomic scale-file write | `test_vit_fp8_scaling.py` skipped the whole module without FlashInfer/cuDNN, so commit 2 had no test on ROCm |
| 5 | Test padded FP8 ViT attention in the encoder CUDA graph layout | Graph replays with pad 128 run the hd128 kernel on zero-length `cu_seqlens` slots, rows past the last image and a buffer-sized `max_seqlen`; the existing varlen test covers packed sequences only |

Commits 1 and 3 work together: the asm kernel needs head_dim 128 (commit 1) and receives the descales only in the shape commit 3 passes. Sequence-parallel MiniMax ViT, previously part of this PR, is split back out to #65311: it showed no measured gain on top of 1+3.

## Claims

- ViT FP8 attention for one 2048x1600 image on MI355X: **2.41 -> 1.32 ms** per layer, including the quantize and slice (the attention kernel alone: 2.30 -> 1.24 ms). That is about 35 ms less encoder time per image over the tower's 32 layers.
- MiniMax-M3 VL serving, MI355X, TP2, 8 image rows, four A/B pairs against this PR's parent:
  - **2048x1600 images: +5.7% throughput (162.8 -> 172.0 tok/s), mean TTFT −7.4% (3.84 -> 3.55 s), median end-to-end latency −5.9% (5.64 -> 5.31 s)**, better in each of the 4 pairs;
  - **+1.1% throughput over the 8 rows** (geomean). No row is worse than the base beyond its pass-to-pass spread in throughput, median TTFT, P99 TTFT or median TPOT.
- Accuracy unchanged: MMMU val 0.6567 vs 0.6600 (± 0.0148 each).
- No TTFT change on 512x512 and 768x1024 images. One metric moves the other way on 2048x1600: median TPOT is higher while mean, P90 and P99 TPOT and end-to-end latency improve. This is explained below.

## Validation

**Serving A/B** (MiniMax-M3 VL `amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4-AttnFP8`, one MI355X node, TP2):
- A = this PR's parent (67791dd94); B = this branch with `VLLM_ROCM_VIT_FP8_PAD_HEAD_DIM=128`. Both run on the vLLM nightly-40941f2c image plus the dtype line of #65352. Without #65352, TP2 start-up with `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data` hangs on this commit range.
- Common settings: OOB TP2 image config, FP8 ViT attention with static scales, `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data`, encoder CUDA graphs (budgets 64–3072). Only the image and that variable differ.
- 8 passes in 4 A/B pairs, 8/8 rows complete in every pass. Each value is the geomean of an arm's 4 passes; positive = B better (throughput B/A − 1, latencies A/B − 1). In brackets: the largest pass-to-pass spread within an arm, in %.

| row (image, ISL, conc) | throughput | median TTFT | mean TTFT | P99 TTFT | median TPOT | E2E |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 512x512, 1024, c16 | +0.4% (1) | −9.6% (46) | −1.3% (5) | +0.4% (2) | +0.5% (2) | +0.3% (2) |
| 768x1024, 1024, c16 | −0.2% (3) | +5.0% (51) | +0.8% (20) | −0.7% (6) | −1.5% (18) | +0.7% (3) |
| **2048x1600, 1024, c16** | **+5.7%** (5) | **+10.8%** (18) | **+8.0%** (6) | +4.3% (15) | −0.5% (117) | **+6.2%** (3) |
| 768x1024, 256, c16 | +0.9% (1) | −2.1% (36) | −1.6% (15) | +1.8% (4) | +3.6% (10) | +0.2% (5) |
| 768x1024, 8192, c16 | −0.0% (1) | +6.5% (124) | +4.2% (76) | +0.6% (1) | −6.0% (134) | +0.3% (1) |
| 768x1024, 1024, c4 | +0.7% (2) | +1.6% (2) | −0.8% (7) | +0.8% (3) | +1.4% (4) | +0.6% (1) |
| 768x1024, 1024, c64 | +1.1% (1) | +23.1% (176) | +10.9% (78) | +1.9% (3) | −10.3% (77) | +0.8% (2) |
| 768x1024, 1024, c256 | +0.6% (0) | +0.5% (1) | +0.7% (0) | +1.0% (1) | +0.5% (1) | +0.6% (1) |
| **8-row geomean** | **+1.1%** | +4.1% | +2.5% | +1.3% | −1.7% | **+1.2%** |

The c16/c64 rows are closed loop: 16 or 64 clients, each sending its next request when its last one completes. On these rows median TTFT and median TPOT split an unchanged end-to-end time, and the split moves between passes of the same build (see the large spreads in brackets). **Mean TTFT, P99 TTFT and E2E are the stable measures there.**

**Small and mid-size images: no TTFT change.**
- In a quieter A/B (4 pairs measured side by side, each pass starting with a warm-up row, no server start during the rows), 512x512 median TTFT is 344 ms on the base and 351 ms with this PR (−2.1%, within an 8% spread), at 1.88 vs 1.87 s E2E.
- 768x1024 c16 and c64: median TTFT +3.4% / +1.4%, E2E −0.0% / +0.7%.
- An earlier single-node A/B had shown higher median TTFT on these rows. It did not reproduce. Those rows were measured first after a server start (vLLM compiles some kernels on the first requests of each new shape) or while another server on the node was starting.

**2048x1600 median TPOT: higher, while the rest of the TPOT distribution improves.**
- In the quieter A/B, median TPOT goes 20.5 -> 24.6 ms, while P90 TPOT goes 77 -> 72 ms, P99 93 -> 88 ms, and mean stays 31.1 vs 31.6 ms. E2E is 6.9% lower at the median, P90 and P99.
- Per-request inter-token latencies show plain decode steps unchanged (10.5 vs 10.4 ms), and the same number and total length of prefill stalls per request (steps that encode and prefill other requests' images).
- The closed-loop benchmark batches the faster-returning requests' prefills differently, so the median request's single stall is longer (about 830 vs 575 ms). The base's own median TPOT on this row ranges 16.6–26.7 ms across runs.

**TP4** (one 8-row pair, then 2 pairs of the 512x512, 768x1024 c16/c64 and 2048x1600 rows side by side): 2048x1600 throughput +8.6% / +6.7%, E2E +9.3% / +7.5%; the other rows −1.0% to +2.4% throughput. 768x1024 c16 mean TTFT is 3–7% higher in all three TP4 pairs, within the pass-to-pass spread, at equal throughput and E2E and lower P99 TTFT.

**Per commit** (same node, leave-one-out: the 4 B passes against one pass without the commit; 2048x1600 row):
- commit 1 (pad to 128; without it, pad 16): +4.3% throughput, +4.8% E2E. A separate 3-pair pad-16 vs pad-128 A/B on the same image gave +7.7%.
- commit 3 (descales of shape `(1,)`; without it, AITER runs CK-tile at head_dim 128): +3.4% throughput, +3.7% E2E. It also gives +1.1% to +2.1% throughput on five of the six 768x1024 rows, because padding without the asm kernel costs a little.
- commit 2 is a correctness fix and is not expected to change performance.

**Accuracy:** MMMU val (900 questions, greedy, TP2): A 0.6600, B 0.6567 (± 0.0148 each); the difference is 0.16 of its standard error. An earlier pair on another node gave A 0.6533, B 0.6444. Zero padding leaves the attention scores unchanged in exact arithmetic; only the kernel's rounding differs. Static FP8 scales calibrated with commit 2 give 0.6422, against 0.6456 for BF16 ViT attention.

**Tests:** on MI355X, `tests/kernels/core/test_vit_fp8_quant.py`, `test_vit_fp8_scaling.py`, `test_vit_fp8_attn.py` and `tests/kernels/attention/test_mha_attn.py` give **77 passed, 13 skipped, 0 failed**, both with default padding and with `VLLM_ROCM_VIT_FP8_PAD_HEAD_DIM=128`. All 13 skips need FlashInfer or cuDNN.
- `test_mha_attn_aiter_fp8_pad_head_dim` (new) runs pad 16 and 128 on two layouts: packed sequences, and the encoder CUDA graph layout (zero-length `cu_seqlens` slots up to the graph's batch size, rows past the last sequence, `max_seqlen` baked to the buffer rows). It checks the head_dim the kernel is launched with, and checks the real rows against the reference.
- `test_vit_fp8_scaling.py` now runs on ROCm; its FlashInfer tests skip themselves. It includes two CPU tests of commit 2's write:
  - one rename of a complete temporary file, nothing left behind, one-shot by default;
  - rewritten at every wrap with `VLLM_MM_ENCODER_FP8_SCALE_SAVE_EVERY_WRAP=1`.

`pre-commit run` on the changed files passes.

## Details

- **Why the descale shape matters:** AITER selects the asm FP8 kernel only when the descales arrive as 1-element tensors of shape `(1,)` and head_dim is 128. Otherwise it falls back to CK-tile, which is about 1.7x slower at 16k patches.
- **Why the gain follows image size:** attention cost grows with the square of the patches per image. A 2048x1600 image is 16,416 patches, a 768x1024 image 4,144 and a 512x512 image 1,444. Inside the encoder CUDA graphs:
  - the asm kernel is 0.44 ms faster per 768x1024 replay (one image) and 2.6 ms faster per two-image replay;
  - it is about 0.3 ms slower per 512x512 replay;
  - both effects are too small to show end to end.
- **Padding cost:** padding 80 to 128 spends compute on zero columns. A native head_dim-80 asm kernel would avoid it.
- **Interaction with encoder CUDA graph work:** the padded kernel runs inside encoder graph replays (commit 5 tests that layout). It is independent of #65084/#65227, which change budgets and capture.
- **Overlap:** #60809 also edits `mm_encoder_attention.py`; the two are independent. No other open PR changes these code paths.
- **AI assistance:** AI assistance was used to write the code and tests, run the experiments and draft this description. The submitter reviewed every changed line and the results.

---

</details>

files.patch:
@@ -437,6 +437,105 @@ def test_mha_attn_varlen_forward_aiter_fp8(
         vllm_config.model_config = old_model_config
 
 
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.is_rocm() or not on_mi3xx(),
+    reason="AITER FP8 attention requires MI300/MI350",
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("pad_head_dim", [16, 128])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "layout",
+    [
+        # (sequence lengths, rows, cu_seqlens slots, max_seqlen)
+        ([2304, 2048], 4352, 2, 2304),
+        # As an encoder CUDA graph replays: zero-length trailing slots up to
+        # max_batch_size, rows past the last sequence, max_seqlen baked to the
+        # buffer rows.
+        ([2304, 2048], 4608, 64, 4608),
+    ],
+    ids=["eager", "graph"],
+)
+def test_mha_attn_aiter_fp8_pad_head_dim(
+    default_vllm_config,
+    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
+    pad_head_dim: int,
+    layout: tuple[list[int], int, int, int],
+):
+    """VLLM_ROCM_VIT_FP8_PAD_HEAD_DIM=128 pads head_dim 80 to 128 in the eager
+    and in the encoder CUDA graph layout; the real rows match the reference
+    either way."""
+    aiter = pytest.importorskip("aiter")
+    if not hasattr(aiter, "flash_attn_varlen_fp8_pertensor_func"):
+        pytest.skip("Installed AITER does not provide varlen FP8 attention")
+    import vllm.model_executor.layers.attention.mm_encoder_attention as mm_attn
+
+    monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_ROCM_VIT_FP8_PAD_HEAD_DIM", str(pad_head_dim))
+    var_seq_len, num_rows, num_slots, max_seqlen = layout
+    num_heads, head_size = 16, 80
+    set_random_seed(0)
+    torch.set_default_device("cuda")
+    torch.set_default_dtype(torch.bfloat16)
+
+    vllm_config = get_current_vllm_config()
+    old_model_config = vllm_config.model_config
+    vllm_config.model_config = type(
+        "MinimalModelConfig",
+        (),
+        {
+            "multimodal_config": MultiModalConfig(
+                mm_encoder_attn_backend=AttentionBackendEnum.ROCM_AITER_FA,
+                mm_encoder_attn_dtype="fp8",
+            ),
+        },
+    )()
+    try:
+        real_len = sum(var_seq_len)
+        offsets = [0, *itertools.accumulate(var_seq_len)]
+        offsets += [real_len] * (num_slots + 1 - len(offsets))
+        qkv = torch.randn(1, num_rows, 3, num_heads, head_size)
+        q, k, v = qkv.unbind(dim=2)
+        cu_seqlens = torch.tensor(offsets, dtype=torch.int32)
+        scale = 1.0 / head_size**0.5
+
+        attn = MMEncoderAttention(num_heads, head_size, scale=scale)
+        launched_head_dims = []
+        wrapper = mm_attn.vit_aiter_fp8_attn_wrapper
+
+        def spy(**kwargs):
+            launched_head_dims.append(kwargs["q"].shape[-1])
+            return wrapper(**kwargs)
+
+        monkeypatch.setattr(mm_attn, "vit_aiter_fp8_attn_wrapper", spy)
+        output = attn(
+            q,
+            k,
+            v,
+            cu_seqlens=cu_seqlens,
+            max_seqlen=torch.tensor(max_seqlen, dtype=torch.int32, device="cpu"),
+        )
+
+        assert launched_head_dims == [128 if pad_head_dim == 128 else head_size]
+        assert output.shape == (1, num_rows, num_heads, head_size)
+        output = output[:, :real_len].float()
+        ref_output = torch.cat(
+            [
+                ref_attention(q_i, k_i, v_i, scale=scale)
+                for q_i, k_i, v_i in zip(
+                    torch.split(q[:, :real_len], var_seq_len, dim=1),
+                    torch.split(k[:, :real_len], var_seq_len, dim=1),
+                    torch.split(v[:, :real_len], var_seq_len, dim=1),
+                )
+            ],
+            dim=1,
+        ).float()
+        cosine = torch.nn.functional.cosine_similarity(
+            output.flatten(), ref_output.flatten(), dim=0
+        )
+        assert cosine.item() >= 0.99
+        assert (output - ref_output).abs().max().item() <= 0.30
+    finally:
+        vllm_config.model_config = old_model_config
+
